slides.title: Towards Agentic Agent-based Models: Feasibility, Performance, and Statistical Model Checking
slides.tldr: INTEGRATING LLM-BASED AGENTS INTO ABM SIMULATIONS
slides.highlight: This research explores the feasibility and reliability of replacing symbolic rules in agent-based models with LLM-driven decisions, which is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Investigates the feasibility and impact of replacing symbolic rules in Agent-Based Models with LLM-driven tool calls.
card.key_idea: Extends the Schelling segregation model by delegating one agent's neighbor classification to a local LLM (Qwen3.5) using tool calls to update similarity counters.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via robustness checks on Qwen3.5 (0.8b-9b) and statistical model checking with MultiVeStA to compare original vs. LLM-extended model trajectories.
card.limitation: Small LLMs exhibit semantic and operational failures; larger models are reliable but introduce significant computational runtime overhead.

slides.title: MeetingToM: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs on Theory-of-Mind Reasoning in Multi-Party Meetings
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR MULTIMODAL THEORY-OF-MIND REASONING IN MEETINGS
slides.highlight: This work introduces MeetingToM to evaluate MLLMs on subject-level mental states, addressee understanding, and group consensus, supporting HyECHO's goals in multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: MeetingToM evaluates MLLMs' ability to reason about latent social states and group dynamics in multi-party meetings.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical benchmark featuring three tasks: subject-level mental state prediction, dyadic addressee/attitude inference, and group-level consensus reasoning, specifically targeting 'pseudo-consensus' where verbal agreement masks dissent.
card.evaluation: Tested proprietary (GPT-5, Gemini-3 Pro) and open-source (Qwen) MLLMs using 1,800 clips from the AMI Corpus; humans significantly outperformed models.
card.limitation: Limited to English-language meetings, short video segments (5s/50s) rather than full meetings, and lacks participant self-reported mental states.

slides.title: PACE: Persona Adaptation through Conversational Elicitation in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: DYNAMIC PERSONA ADAPTATION FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for humanoid robots to dynamically synthesize tailored, psychologically grounded personas through user interaction, supporting the RwB goal of enhancing human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: PACE enables humanoid robots to dynamically generate personalized personas through interactive Q&A with users.
card.key_idea: An elicitation pipeline uses adaptive Q&A to build a psychologically grounded PersonaSpec, which is compiled into system prompts and mapped to Ameca robot's multimodal behaviors.
card.evaluation: Tested with 25 participants against a static baseline using BFI-44, economic games, and Likert scales; PACE showed significant gains in fidelity and interaction quality.
card.limitation: Relies on cloud-based inference and ASR, potentially introducing latency and transcription errors in noisy environments.

slides.title: On the Structure of Address in Multi-Party Dialogue: From Discrete Labels to Continuous Levels
slides.tldr: CONTINUOUS ADDRESSEE DETECTION IN MULTI-PARTY DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: This research explores addressee detection as a continuous phenomenon rather than a discrete classification task, analyzing its relationship with gaze and backchannels. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: Address in multi-party dialogue is better modeled as a continuous level than as discrete labels.
card.key_idea: A latent-variable model transforms categorical annotator labels into continuous address levels, representing addressivity as a graded property rather than a multi-class classification task.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a Japanese triadic dialogue corpus using Bayesian mixed-effects models; continuous levels showed better predictive fit (ELPD) for turn-taking, gaze, and backchannels.
card.limitation: Data is limited to Japanese triadic discussions; address levels were inferred from only three categorical annotations per turn.

slides.title: S.E.A.G.R: A Socially and Emotionally Aware Greeting Robot Framework with Dual-Layer Cultural and Affective Modulation
slides.tldr: CULTURALLY AND EMOTIONALLY ADAPTIVE GREETING FRAMEWORK
slides.highlight: This framework introduces a dual-layer modulation system for greeting robots that adapts based on cultural identity and affective cues, supporting the RwB goal of enhancing human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A robotic greeting framework that adapts gesture type by culture and execution by user emotion.
card.key_idea: A dual-layer Sense–Think–Act architecture: Layer 1 selects culturally appropriate greetings via badge ID; Layer 2 modulates gesture amplitude and duration based on detected facial expressions.
card.evaluation: Implemented as a low-cost proof-of-concept prototype using Arduino and Python; no empirical user studies were conducted.
card.limitation: Lacks empirical validation through user studies and relies on badge-based identification, which does not generalize to all public spaces.

slides.title: How Reliable Are Multimodal Signals of Conversational State? Evidence from Remote Dyadic Collaborative Tasks
slides.tldr: EVALUATING MULTIMODAL SIGNALS FOR CONVERSATIONAL STATE
slides.highlight: This research evaluates the reliability of linguistic, acoustic, and interaction features for predicting cognitive load and power roles, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Multimodal signals of conversational state often lack generalizability and reliability once speaker identity is controlled.
card.key_idea: A three-dimensional framework (predictive accuracy, cross-task generalizability, and test-retest reliability) evaluating interactional, acoustic, and linguistic features in remote dyadic collaborative tasks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on AVCAffe dataset (53 dyads, 9 tasks) using LODO cross-validation, LOCO analysis, and ICC before/after speaker normalization.
card.limitation: Conversational power prediction remained near chance; results are limited to Zoom-mediated dyadic interactions and task-level aggregation.

slides.title: Imitation of Arm Gestures by the Semi-Humanoid Robot NICO
slides.tldr: HUMAN ARM GESTURE IMITATION FOR SEMI-HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work presents a system for a semi-humanoid robot to imitate human arm gestures using a pose-estimation model and analytical geometry, contributing to the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A system for the NICO robot to imitate human arm gestures using monocular RGB input.
card.key_idea: Combines MediaPipe pose and hand landmark extraction with analytical geometry to compute joint angles, which are then linearly mapped to NICO's specific motor configurations.
card.evaluation: Tested with six participants across 11 poses and three viewing angles. Results show moderate accuracy for most joints, with MAEs between 10° and 34°.
card.limitation: High reconstruction error for forearm rotation (50.1° MAE) and sensitivity to self-occlusions and complex wrist-related movements.

slides.title: Modeling turn-taking with distant viewing: investigating silence thresholds in human and AI-generated discourse
slides.tldr: ANALYSIS OF SILENCE GAPS IN HUMAN AND AI DISCOURSE
slides.highlight: This study examines silence thresholds and turn-taking in human and AI-generated audiovisual material, contributing to the understanding of engagement and social perception for HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Study compares silence gaps in human sitcoms versus AI-generated podcasts to analyze turn-taking patterns.
card.key_idea: Analysis of silence thresholds across speaker gender and production settings using thirty US sitcoms and fifty-one Google NotebookLM synthetic podcasts.
card.evaluation: Analyzed audiovisual material using Praat for fundamental-frequency gender estimation; results compare human and AI-generated discourse.

slides.title: Chinese AI Brand Launches World’s First Humanoid Robot Fight League
slides.highlight: The launch of a humanoid robot fight league provides insights into the physical capabilities and interaction dynamics of humanoid systems, relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.
